question: What is the primary financial mechanism by which an individual secures coverage through an HMO?
explanation: Enrollees secure their healthcare coverage by paying a predictable, recurring fee called a premium, which transfers the financial risk of illness to the HMO. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of utilizing a primary care physician as a gatekeeper within an HMO structure?

options.A: To collect insurance premiums directly from enrolled patients
options.B: To determine government health policy and funding allocations
options.C: To audit hospital pharmacies for expired pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: To coordinate care and prevent unnecessary specialist visits

explanation: The gatekeeper model ensures that routine health issues are managed at the primary level before escalating resources to costly specialists. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h1)

question: What has been the historically dominant method of paying for healthcare services in Nigeria prior to widespread HMO adoption?
explanation: Patients traditionally paid cash directly at the point of service for consultations, diagnostics, and medications, creating severe financial barriers to care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: How do HMOs primarily protect enrollees from catastrophic financial ruin during major illness?

options.A: By loaning money directly to hospitals for infrastructural development
options.B: By forcing pharmaceutical companies to lower drug prices by law
options.C: By pooling financial risk across a large population of contributors
options.D: By providing tax exemptions to patients with chronic medical conditions

explanation: Risk pooling collects funds from many people so that the high medical costs of the few who fall ill can be covered without bankrupting individuals. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h2)

question: Which operational model involves an HMO directly employing healthcare providers and owning the clinics where care is delivered?
explanation: In a staff model HMO, the organization owns the healthcare facilities and employs the physicians and clinical staff directly. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the defining characteristic of an Independent Practice Association (IPA) model?

options.A: Patients are restricted to visiting a single multi-specialty government hospital
options.B: Doctors are strictly salaried employees who work exclusively for one HMO
options.C: Physicians maintain their own private practices while contracting with the HMO
options.D: The government directly manages all medical appointments and pharmacy supplies

explanation: IPAs consist of independent doctors who continue running their own offices while agreeing to care for HMO enrollees as part of a collective contract. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the name of the regulatory body responsible for licensing and supervising HMOs in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA) regulates, supervises, and issues operating licenses to HMOs across Nigeria. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which of the following responsibilities does the NHIA hold regarding HMO operations?

options.A: Investigating enrollee complaints and sanctioning non-compliant HMOs
options.B: Setting individual hospital room rates and doctor salaries
options.C: Manufacturing essential generic drugs for hospital dispensaries
options.D: Directly hiring nursing staff for private HMO-owned clinics

explanation: The regulatory agency protects consumers by handling grievances and penalizing HMOs that delay payments or improperly deny patient care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: What term describes the process where a hospital must seek approval from an HMO before performing an expensive elective procedure?
explanation: Prior authorization is a utilization management tool ensuring that high-cost treatments are clinically justified before the insurance plan agrees to pay. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why do HMOs establish tightly managed provider networks rather than allowing patients to visit any hospital freely?

options.A: To control costs and maintain quality control through contractual standards
options.B: To prevent foreign pharmaceutical companies from importing vaccines
options.C: To ensure that nurses work longer shifts without extra compensation
options.D: To eliminate the need for primary care physicians in rural areas

explanation: Networks allow HMOs to negotiate predictable pricing, monitor clinical outcomes, and prevent unnecessary utilization of medical resources. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which payment mechanism involves an HMO paying a healthcare provider a fixed monthly sum per registered patient regardless of service usage?
explanation: Capitation pays providers a predictable flat rate per head, shifting the financial risk of high service utilization onto the clinic or doctor. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is a primary behavioral incentive created for doctors under a capitation payment system?

options.A: To bill the HMO separately for every routine blood pressure check
options.B: To emphasize preventative care and keep enrolled patients healthy
options.C: To order as many diagnostic laboratory tests as possible per visit
options.D: To encourage patients to seek emergency room care frequently

explanation: Since providers keep the flat monthly fee even if the patient stays home, they maximize profit by keeping patients well through disease prevention. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is a major operational challenge frequently experienced in the Nigerian HMO sector?

options.A: Excessive government funding causing severe hospital inflation
options.B: Delayed capitation payments from HMOs to healthcare providers
options.C: Universal coverage achieved for all rural agricultural workers
options.D: Complete absence of private insurance companies nationwide

explanation: Many Nigerian healthcare facilities struggle financially because some HMOs delay or under-remit the monthly capitation funds owed to them. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h7)

question: What is meant by the unethical practice of 'creaming' sometimes observed among contracted healthcare providers?

options.A: Charging patients illegal cash fees for every single prescription drug
options.B: Embezzling corporate premium payments meant for staff salaries
options.C: Refusing to submit monthly medical utilization reports to the NHIA
options.D: Collecting capitation for healthy enrollees while avoiding costly sick patients

explanation: Creaming refers to providers welcoming healthy subscribers to collect easy capitation while discouraging or maltreating patients who need expensive care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h7)

question: What is a primary administrative reason why accurate nursing documentation is crucial in an HMO-managed hospital?

options.A: Nurses are legally required to calculate monthly capitation profits
options.B: Insurance laws mandate that nurses collect premium payments directly
options.C: HMO regulations forbid nurses from administering intravenous drugs
options.D: Incomplete records frequently lead to claim rejections by HMO auditors

explanation: HMO audit teams rely heavily on thorough nursing notes and clinical charts to justify the release of funds for medical services rendered. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h8)

question: How does a nurse case manager directly contribute to the financial sustainability of an HMO-managed care system?

options.A: By negotiating premium pricing contracts directly with corporate employers
options.B: By manufacturing essential generic pharmaceuticals within the hospital ward
options.C: By coordinating outpatient care for chronic patients to prevent costly hospital admissions
options.D: By penalizing clinics that fail to disburse staff salaries on time

explanation: Proactive outpatient management of chronic conditions keeps patients stable at home, preventing expensive inpatient admissions that drain insurance funds. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h8)
